summary.text: From age 55, you can withdraw any OA amount if you have set aside your FRS. Otherwise, you can withdraw $5,000 from your OA.

details.heading: Check your available amount
details.body: Log into your Retirement dashboard to check how much CPF savings you can withdraw from age 55.

details.heading: If you have set aside your FRS
details.body: If your Full Retirement Sum is set aside fully in cash, or with a mixture of property and cash, you can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account.

details.heading: If you have not set aside your FRS
details.body: You can withdraw $5,000 from your Ordinary Account. After you withdraw, non-withdrawable OA savings may be transferred to your Retirement Account to help make up your FRS.

sources.page_title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 55 to 64?

quotes.text: The amount that you can withdraw is determined as follows:
You can check the CPF savings you can withdraw from age 55 by logging into your Retirement dashboard.
If you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash: You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA)

If you have not set aside your FRS: You can withdraw $5,000 from your OA Upon your withdrawal, non-withdrawable amounts in your OA may be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to make up your FRS.
